A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Relational Transformer research. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved between appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original RelBench zero-shot and supervised learning results, learning curves, and context and architecture ablations in Sections 4–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds frozen-feature experiments, inference-cost measurements, attention-order ablations, and database heterogeneity analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4.4 adds an adaptation procedure that freezes RT and trains a two-layer MLP on its masked-token representations. The core tokenization, sampling algorithm, attention components, losses, and default transformer block remain unchanged. Renaming task table integration to task table prompting does not change that mechanism.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same RelBench databases, autocomplete tasks, and forecasting evaluation comprising 10 classification and eight regression tasks, excluding rel-event from evaluation. The new studies reuse this coverage; the added RelBench v2 citation does not establish evaluation on additional datasets.

E2.justification: New Table 3 introduces frozen untrained GNN and untrained RT representations with trained MLPs as comparison variants for pretrained RT feature extraction. Comparator membership in the original zero-shot and full fine-tuning comparisons is retained.

E3.justification: The original splits, training budgets, and prediction metrics remain, but v3 substantially expands evaluation design. It adds MLP-only adaptation, A100 latency and memory measurements across RT context lengths of 256–1024 and Griffin sampling configurations, and comparisons of sequential versus parallel attention arrangements.

E4.justification: v3 adds analyses of frozen representation quality, performance sensitivity to inference context size, six attention-layer orders plus parallel attention, and whether schema overlap or feature distributions could explain transfer. These substantially broaden the supplementary evidence. Existing context-removal, attention-removal, and multi-cell-masking ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, performance confidence intervals, or significance tests. The mean and standard deviation reporting for sampled context-label counts is unchanged, moving from v1 Table 9 to v3 Table 12.

E6.justification: Substantial results are added for feature extraction, inference costs, attention ordering, and database heterogeneity. Under the same stated zero-shot settings, Table 1 changes RT mean AUROC from 70.1 to 69.7 without target-database pretraining and from 72.9 to 71.9 with it. Table 2 changes unseen-database mean R2 from 22.8 to 22.7. Original full fine-tuning and ablation values remain; the numerical revisions are not explained.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 corrects attention masking: v1 multiplies logits by a binary mask before softmax, whereas v3 explicitly assigns negative infinity to disallowed entries. This is a substantive mathematical correction matching the stated visibility semantics. The symmetry and expressivity discussion in v3 Appendix E already appeared in v1 Appendix C.1; no new proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The headline quantitative transfer claim is narrowed: the abstract changes from 94% to 93% of supervised AUROC, and the introduction changes 90.8%/94.4% to 90.3%/93.1%. The central claims about schema-agnostic pretraining, zero-shot transfer, sample efficiency, and strong fine-tuning performance remain.

C2.justification: New Appendix C argues that database heterogeneity excludes lexical similarity and dataset shortcuts as explanations for transfer. Section 4.5 adds explanations for RT's computational advantage, and Section 2.3 elaborates practical applicability. These supplement the retained transfer interpretations; the stated limitations concerning recommendation, link prediction, and foreign-key semantics remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix I.1 newly discloses EntityMean's training-set global-mean fallback and evaluation on a subsampled test set, without establishing that these procedures changed. Figure 6 specifies its illustrative sampler settings, and the new cost plots identify evaluation hardware and batch size. The existing repository footnote now explicitly identifies code, models, and data.

R1.justification: v3 adds the RelBench v2 reference and changes the appendix description of KumoRFM from zero-shot to in-context learning capabilities, aligning it with the main-text distinction. Most citations and positioning against tabular, graph, and relational foundation models are retained.

P1.justification: v3 adds a dedicated zero-shot-learning explanation, consistently adopts task table prompting terminology, moves context sampling earlier in the appendices, and separates the existing symmetry discussion. Publication headers and affiliations also change. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain closely matched.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the visual presentation with a four-panel cost-quality figure, a graph-and-table context illustration, and new feature-extraction, schema-similarity, and attention-order tables. Existing displays are retained but extensively repositioned and repacked, with table captions generally moved below the tables.

improvement.justification: v3 improves practical assessment through frozen-feature and inference-cost experiments, adds useful sensitivity analyses, and corrects the masking equation. These gains are tempered by unreconciled differences between updated zero-shot tables and retained ablation baselines. Appendix C also draws stronger conclusions about excluding shortcuts than its descriptive analyses establish. Overall, the additions provide a limited net improvement.
